title: L4/L7 load balancer vs API gateway vs Kubernetes Service
description: Three ingress/compute membership hops. None of them is a primary store or a fencing token.

cells.workload: Spread TCP/HTTP across healthy backends. Connection or request dispatch.
cells.consistency: No data consistency. Session affinity is a routing hint, not a shard map.
cells.latency: Sub-ms to a few ms plus health-check lag for membership.
cells.scaling: Horizontal backends. Cross-AZ balancer is still one region unless you say otherwise.
cells.failure: Unhealthy member drained after check interval. Dead member can still get traffic during TTL of the check.
cells.costOps: Cheap relative to compute. Need health, TLS policy, and capacity headroom.
cells.whenNot: When you needed a uniqueness boundary, a ledger, or multi-region failover. A VIP is not fencing.

cells.workload: Authn, rate limit, request shaping, protocol translation in front of services.
cells.consistency: Authz decisions are per request. Cached JWKS/keys can be stale.
cells.latency: Adds hops; p99 includes auth and quota checks.
cells.scaling: Stateless replicas plus a quota store. The quota store has its own consistency story.
cells.failure: Gateway outage is a total brownout unless you have a bypass that you named.
cells.costOps: Policy cardinality and cert rotation dominate. Misconfigured rate limits amplify retries.
cells.whenNot: Putting the TokenX ledger in the gateway. Gateways authorize; they do not settle.

cells.workload: Process placement and kube-proxy/IPVS/Envoy membership for pods.
cells.consistency: Endpoint slices lag. Not a data model.
cells.latency: Cluster DNS + kube-proxy. Not a substitute for a regional LB at the edge.
cells.scaling: HPA/VPA change replica counts from derived metrics. Scale-to-zero drops in-flight work.
cells.failure: Pod death is SIGTERM + grace; not lossless. Cluster control plane loss is a different failure.
cells.costOps: Control plane, node pools, and HPA flapping cost real money.
cells.whenNot: Treating replica count as RPO=0 or using etcd as your application database.

assumptions: Single region unless a cell says otherwise.
Balancer membership is derived from health checks; stale members receive traffic until the check fails.
Kubernetes replica count is not durability of in-flight requests.
